description: The public benchmark corpus: sentences anyone may rerun through a dictation app. Every sentence was written for this corpus or taken from a sentence the repository already carries (the take's source says which). Every person, place and product named is either a public product name or invented for this corpus. benchmark_public.py speaks each take with a macOS system voice on the machine running it; no audio is stored here. docs/benchmarks/public-benchmark.md is the method.

licence.text: AGPL-3.0-only, as the rest of this repository (LICENSE_POLICY.md)
licence.audio: Not distributed. The audio is synthesised on the machine that runs the benchmark with that machine's macOS system voices, whose output is governed by Apple's macOS licence, not by this repository.

privacy: No recording, no owner data, no dictation history: written text and public or invented names only.

takes.text: For the release notes, please say that the Zephyrine update moves storage from the old file format to PostgreSQL, adds a Grafana dashboard for sync errors, and signs people in with OAuth instead of a password. It also fixes the crash that Wojciech reported when a Kubernetes node restarts in the middle of an upload. We tested it for two weeks on the staging cluster and saw no data loss.

takes.text: Notes from today's planning meeting. The team agreed to finish the TypeScript rewrite before starting anything new. Niamh will own the parser, Tadhg will handle the tests, and Aoife will review every pull request before it is merged. We will check progress again on Thursday afternoon. The main risk is that the old code has very few tests, so we may find bugs that nobody knew about. If that happens, we will write them down and decide together which ones to fix first.

takes.text: Here is a summary of the customer call. Kwabena Haddadin from Corvantis said that their team uses Figma for every design and wants to export screens straight into the app. They currently pay $75 a month for a tool that does part of this, and they would switch if we can support comments and version history. Ottoline asked whether they need single sign on, and they said not yet, but probably next year. We agreed to send a short demo video and follow up in two weeks. Overall the call went well, and they seemed genuinely interested in a pilot with around 25 people.
